title: 2D and 3D Shapes (KS1)
subject: Maths
strapline: Flat shapes and solid shapes — and how to describe them.
facts: 2D shapes are flat: circle, triangle, square, rectangle, pentagon (5 sides), hexagon (6 sides).
We describe 2D shapes by their number of sides and corners (vertices).
A triangle has 3 sides; a square has 4 equal sides; a pentagon has 5; a hexagon has 6.
3D shapes are solid: cube, cuboid, sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid.
We describe 3D shapes by faces (flat surfaces), edges and vertices (corners).
A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
A sphere (like a ball) has 1 curved surface and no edges or vertices.

quick_quiz.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
What 3D shape is a tin of beans?
How many faces does a cube have?

teacher_tips: Handle real 3D objects and count faces/edges by touch before using pictures.
Watch for children who only recognise a "square" sitting flat — rotate it.
Use the correct words (vertices, faces) from the start; children cope well.
